contexts.markdownDescription:
Types of symbols to search

Specifies a comma delimited list of [symbol contexts](https://doc.log10x.com/run/transform/symbol/#contexts) values. This is argument is passed as the `symbolContexts` argument value for the [symbolSequence](https://doc.log10x.com/api/js/#TenXObject+symbolSequence) function.  The listed contexts are evaluated in a single pass, so list order acts as a filter rather than a precedence chain. (Default: log,exec)

maxLen.markdownDescription:
Max number of output chars

Specifies the max number of chars of the [symbolMessageField](https://doc.log10x.com/run/initialize/message/#symbolmessagefield). Set 0 to unlimited. (Accepts number or string with $= prefix for runtime evaluation) (Default: 0)

field.markdownDescription:
Field name to assign with symbol sequence value

Specifies the name of the field to assign the return value of [symbolSequence](https://doc.log10x.com/api/js/#TenXObject+symbolSequence) function when invoking it with the a symbolContext argument value of [symbolContexts](https://doc.log10x.com/run/initialize/message/#symbolcontexts).  For an example, see [symbolInputField](https://doc.log10x.com/run/initialize/message/#symbolinputfield). (Default: symbolMessage)

hashField.markdownDescription:
Field name to assign with the hash of the symbol sequence value

Specifies the name of the field to assign a stable, URL-safe hash of the [symbolMessageField](https://doc.log10x.com/run/initialize/message/#symbolmessagefield) value, computed via [TenXString.hash](https://doc.log10x.com/api/js/#TenXString.hash).  The value is an 11-character base64url identifier (xxHash64 of the UTF-8 bytes, big-endian, no padding). It is one-way and reproduces byte-for-byte outside the engine, so it is safe to use directly as a deduplication key, metric dimension, analyzer query term, or forwarder filter key.  **Unset by default.** The enrichment field itself is always present on the TenXObject under the internal name `tenx_hash`, so metrics dimensions, the aggregation key and the MCP artifacts carry the pattern hash whether or not this option is set. What the option controls is the *wire* name, and with it whether the hash reaches a coupled log forwarder: on the [forwarder receive path](https://doc.log10x.com/run/input/forwarder/) the record goes back to the forwarder byte-for-byte as it arrived unless this option names a field, and then that field is spliced onto the returned record.  Set it to `tenx_hash` to get the historical name, or to any other name to both rename the enrichment field and ship it, for example `symbolMessageHashField my_custom_hash`.

originField.markdownDescription:
Field name to assign with symbol message origin file

Specifies the name of the field to assign the return value of [symbolOrigin](https://doc.log10x.com/api/js/#TenXObject+symbolOrigin) function. (Default: )

skeletonField.markdownDescription:
Field name for the pattern rendering hint (the message shape with one marker per identity token)

When set, each template also carries a `skeleton`: the message region of the log line with `~` standing in for every token that went into the message pattern and `$` for every variable. A consumer holding the pattern and the skeleton reconstructs the original line for display — punctuation, spacing and dropped stopwords included — so a readable pattern needs no access to the logs themselves. Unset (the default) computes and emits nothing.

messageNegators.markdownDescription:
List of strings that, when matched at the start of a log line's text, mark it as low-value continuation/boilerplate that does NOT receive its own message pattern.

A list of strings that, when matched at the start of a log line's text, mark it as a known continuation pattern (e.g., stack trace frame, indented detail, banner) that should not receive its own message pattern.  Negators have two consumers. The message template's gate evaluates them when the event is neither part of a multi-event group (groupSize > 1) nor a group head: in that case, an event still receives a pattern unless it matches a negator. This is the "Hello World vs orphan stack frame" discriminator. The group template's head detection also consults them as a veto BETWEEN the timestamp and severity checks: a negator-prefixed line cannot be promoted to group head by severity inference alone (a token like `info` inside an object dump), so continuation fragments weld into their parent instead of minting orphan heads. Both consumers are inert until this list is configured — there is no default.  - ` ` - any indented line (universal continuation signal). - `	` - any tab-prefixed line (Java/Go stack frames etc.). - `Caused by: ` - Java chained exception (column 0). - `Suppressed: ` - Java suppressed exception (column 0). - `--- End of ` - .NET inner exception marker. - `created by ` - Go goroutine creator. - `#0 `..`#5 ` - PHP stack frames (depth 0-5).
